Problem Statement:
Handle unusual __qualname__ in inspect

<!--
Please note that Rich isn't accepting any new features at this point.

If a feature can be implemented without modifying the core library, then
they should be released as a third-party module. I can accept updates to the
core library that make it easier to extend (think hooks).

Bugfixes are always welcome of course.

Sometimes it is not clear what is a feature and what is a bug fix.
If there is any doubt, please open a discussion first.

-->

<!--
*Are you contributing typo fixes?*

If your PR solely consists of typos, at least one must be in the docs to warrant an addition to CONTRIBUTORS.md
-->

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation / docstrings
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate (see note about typos above).
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

FILES: rich/_inspect.py:103, 253
ROOT CAUSE: `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` can return a non-string object (e.g., a member descriptor) when the object has unusual `__qualname__` implementation (like with `@lru_cache` and `__slots__`). This non-string value is later passed to `Text.assemble` or used in an f-string, causing a `TypeError` or incorrect representation.
CHANGE: 
1. In `_get_signature`, change `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` to check if the result is a string, falling back to `__name__` and then to `name`.
2. In `get_object_types_mro_as_strings`, ensure `__qualname__` is a string before using it in the f-string.

Example for `_get_signature`:
```python
qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
if not isinstance(qualname, str):
    qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
if not isinstance(qualname, str):
    qualname = str(qualname)
```
Actually, based on the issue description: "checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback."

For `get_object_types_mro_as_strings`:
The current implementation is `f'{getattr(type_, "__module__", "")}.{getattr(type_, "__qualname__", "")}'`.
If `__qualname__` is not a string, `f-string` will call `__str__`, which might be acceptable, but for consistency and to avoid weird results, we should verify it's a string or ensure it's converted. However, the main crash is in `Text.assemble` in `_get_signature`.

TEST: `python3 repro.py` and `pytest tests/test_inspect.py`

I have fixed the issue where an object with a non-string `__qualname__` (e.g., caused by `@lru_cache` and `__slots__`) would cause `rich.inspect` to fail with a `TypeError`.

Changes:
- In `rich/_inspect.py`, modified `_get_signature` to verify that `qualname` is a string, falling back to `__name__` or a string conversion if it is not.
- In `rich/_inspect.py`, modified `get_object_types_mro_as_strings` to ensure the qualified name used in the MRO string representation is converted to a string if `__qualname__` is not a string.

Verified the fix by running a reproduction script and existing tests:
- `python3 repro.py` now completes successfully.
- `pytest tests/test_inspect.py` passed.
